applicable_when: The kernel has ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing tl.dot to use FP32 FFMA instead of Tensor Cores. Enabling TF32 routes the dot product through the Tensor Core pipeline at ~8x the throughput of scalar FFMA. Additionally, 160 registers/thread (caused by BLOCK_M=128) limits occupancy to 18.75% (only 3 blocks/SM). Reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 64 and BLOCK_N from 16 to 32 cuts register pressure, improves occupancy, and reduces shared-memory bank conflicts by giving the Tensor Core engine a more natural square-tile access pattern. K=3 with BLOCK_K=16 means the K-loop runs exactly once; the primary lever is enabling TF32 Tensor Cores plus reducing BLOCK_M to relieve register pressure.

applicable_when: The kernel is a thin GEMM (M=8M, N=6, K=3) fused with a bias add. BLOCK_M=128 with 160 registers/thread crushes occupancy to 18.75% (Block Limit Registers=3 blocks/SM). The K loop runs only once (ceil(3/16)=1) so BLOCK_K=16 wastes 13 K-slots with masked loads. The 9.5-way shared memory bank conflicts (57.98% speedup) and uncoalesced shared accesses (54.9% speedup) are caused by the large BLOCK_M tile creating strided access patterns in shared memory for the B matrix (stride_bn=3, non-power-of-2). Reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 64 halves register pressure, doubles occupancy, and reduces the shared memory tile footprint that causes bank conflicts. Adding @triton.autotune explores BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, num_warps, and num_stages to find the optimal configuration for this unusual N=6, K=3 shape.
